items.name: datetostr
items.description: Converts date to text. If no format is provided the format of the return text is MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss.  If no time zone is provided the time zone will default to the server's time zone. This method expects the optional dateFormat to be in the same format as used in strtojavadate().
items.syntax: String datetostr(Date date [, String dateFormat [, String timeZone]])
items.example:
Example:
  1.    datetostr (getdate()) will return today's date in the format MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss if no format is supplied

  2.    testDate = strtojavadate("02/03/2010 03-22-55", "MM/dd/yyyy HH-mm-ss");
         dateStr = datetostr(testDate, "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss");
         dateStr now holds the string "2010-02-03 03:22:55"

         The date & time was stored in the server's time zone by default (For this example, assume GMT-8).
         To retrieve the data in another time zone, include the third parameters as string. See the editor's help page for valid time zone inputs.

         datestr = datetostr(testDate, "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss", "GMT-6")
         datestr will return "2010-02-03 01:22:55"

         twelvehour = datetostr(testDate, "yyyy-MM-dd hh:mm:ss a", "GMT+4")
         twelvehour will return "2010-02-03 03:22:55 PM"

  3. The components that can be used to make up a valid date format string are:
      yyyy - Year in long form specifying all digits.
      MM - Month in numeric format
      dd - The day of the month in numeric form e.g 24
      HH - The hour as a number in 24 hour form
      hh - The hour as a number in 12 hour form
      mm - Minutes
      ss - Seconds
      a - AM/PM
      z - General Time Zone
      Z - RFC 822 Time Zone

items.name: strtodate

items.example:
1. If the str value is empty string then strtodate returns ERROR_DATE which in 01/01/0001 (MM/DD/YYYY).

2. If there is a parsing error due to mismatch of str value and the format string passed to strtodate function then the same ERROR_DATE is returned.

3. The components that can be used to make up a valid date format string are:
    %Y - Year in long form specifying all digits.
    %m - Month in numeric format
    %d - The day of the month in numeric form e.g 24
    %H - The hour as a number in 24 hour form
    %M - Minutes
    %S - Seconds
    %T - Time. This is a shorter way of writing a time component in the form %H:%M:%S

Example: strtodate("10/10/2008", "%m/%d/%Y") returns a date object representing October 10, 2010.
4. By default, the date will save to the server's time zone. The Date can be created with a predefined time zone, provided that the correct time zone id is entered.
    See the editor's help page for valid time zone inputs.
    Example:

    To Convert to US Format:
    strtodate("02/12/2010", "%m/%d/%Y") returns a date object representing February 12th, 2010.

    To Convert to European Format:
    strtodate("01/02/2010", "%d/%m/%Y") returns a date object representing February 1st, 2010.

    To Convert to European Format w/ Paris, France time zone
    parisdate = strtodate("01/02/2010 16:30:40", "%d/%m/%Y %H:%M:%S", "Europe/Paris") returns a date object representing February 1st, 2010 with a time zone in Paris France.

    When the datetostr method is used, another time zone can be specified and will render with the appropriate time difference.
    datetostr(parisdate, "dd/MM/yyyy %H:%M:%S", "America/Chicago") will display "01/02/2010 09:30:40"

items.name: gettabledata
items.description: Returns a 2-D array of String containing data table data matching the condition specified.
items.syntax: String[][] gettabledata(String tableName, String[] selectColumns, [String[] whereClauseColumns, String[] whereClauseValues, [String[] whereClauseComps, [boolean whereClauseUseORs]]])
items.example:
Deprecated: This function is vulnerable to SQL injection and its usage is discouraged. Use BMQL() instead. Please refer to the site documentation for further details.

1. Following comparators are supported by the gettabledata BML function:
"=", "<>", "<", ">", "<=", ">=", and "like".

When the whereClauseComps parameter is not specified, it is assumed to the "="
4. whereClauseUseORs: When this is false (default) all the conditions are logically AND'ed i.e. they form (condition1 AND condition2 AND condition3...). When this parameter is true then the conditions are logically OR'ed i.e. they form (condition1 OR condition2 OR condition3...)

Example:
Assume you have a data table with four columns: color, shape, length and area. To get data from this table, frame your query as follows
selectColumns = string[]{"color","shape"};
whereClauseColumns = string[]{"length", "area"};
whereClauseValues = integer[]{10, 300};
whereClauseComps = string[]{">", "<"};
doubleArr = gettabledata("my_table", selectColumns, whereClauseColumns, whereClauseValues, whereClauseComps);
This will return a 2-D array with the color and the shape columns when length > 10 and area < 300

items.name: bmql
items.description: Queries a data table to retrieve records, insert new rows, change existing rows or delete rows.
items.syntax: RecordSet bmql(String sqlQuery [, String Dictionary contextOverride, String Dictionary fieldMap])
items.example:
Usage (Select Example):
    results = bmql("select part_number from _parts where part_number = 'part%'");
    for result in results {
        partno = get(result, "part_number");
        ...
    }

For SELECT statements, 'results' is returned by bmql which contains the list of data that matched the query.
for loop can be used on 'results' to go through all the rows of data returned.
'get' function can be used to get the specific column from each row we iterate.


Usage (Insert Example):
    results = bmql("insert into table1 (column1, column2) values ('value1', 11),('value2', 22)");
    for result in results {
        insert_count_integer = get(result, "records_inserted");
        records_error_string = get(result, "records_error");
    }

For INSERT statements, 'results' is a record set with one integer entry that indicates the number of rows added. This is usually the same as the number of records in the VALUES part of the BMQL statement, but sometimes a row may fail due to duplicate natural key entries.
When this occurs, a 'records_error' key will be added, showing the first record that blocks the insertion, as a JSON string.


Usage (Delete Example):
    results = bmql("delete from table1 where column1 = 'value2'");
    for result in results {
        deletion_count_integer = get(result, "records_deleted");
    }

For DELETE statements, 'results' is a record set with one integer entry that indicates the number of rows deleted.
Executing a DELETE statement without a WHERE clause will clear all of the data in the table.


Usage (Update Example):
    results = bmql("update table1 set colum1 = 'new_value1', column2 = 'new_value2' where column1 = 'old_value1'");
    for result in results {
        update_count_integer = get(result, "records_updated");
        records_error_string = get(result, "records_error");
    }

Results will be a record set with one integer entry, showing the number of rows modified.
A 'records_error' entry also appears when the query is valid, but table state blocks the update.
Executing an UPDATE statement without a WHERE clause will update all of the rows in the table.


Usage (Modify Example):
    results = bmql("modify table1 set colum1 = 'new_value1', column2 = 'new_value2' where column1 = 'old_value1'");
    for result in results {
        insert_count_integer = get(result, "records_inserted");
        update_count_integer = get(result, "records_updated");
        records_error_string = get(result, "records_error");
    }

Results will be a record set with two integer entries, one with the number of rows modified and one with the number of rows added.
A 'records_error' entry also appears when the query is valid, but table state blocks the modification.
The above query will change all records matching the WHERE condition; if no rows match the condition, it will instead add a new row.
Executing a MODIFY statement without a WHERE clause will update all of the rows in the table.

Variables in Query:

    BML variables can be used in the WHERE clause conditions.

    pno = "part123";
    lead = int[] { 3, 4, 5 };
    results = bmql("select part_number from _parts where part_number = $pno and lead_time in $lead");

    1. '$' symbol has to be prepended to the variable name when used in the query string.
    2. The datatypes of the variables should be string, integer or float.
    3. For IN condition the datatypes of the variables should be string[], integer[] or float[].
    4. Line item variables cannot be used in the query.

Select Query:
    SELECT [DISTINCT] field1[, field2, ..., fieldn]
    FROM dataBaseObject
    [WHERE condition]
    [ORDER BY field1 [ASC|DESC],[ field2 [ASC|DESC], ..., fieldn [ASC|DESC]]]

Insert Query:
    INSERT INTO dataBaseObject (column1 [, column2, ..., columnn])
    VALUES (record1_column1 [, record1_column2, ..., record1_columnN])[, (record2_column1 [, record2_column2, ..., record2_columnN)]])

Delete Query:
    DELETE FROM dataBaseObject
    [WHERE condition]

UPDATE Query:
    UPDATE dataBaseObject
    SET field1 = value1 [, field2 = value2, ..., fieldn = valuen]
    [WHERE condition]

MODIFY Query:
    MODIFY dataBaseObject
    SET field1 = value1 [, field2 = value2, ..., fieldn = valuen]
    [WHERE condition]

SELECT, INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE and MODIFY keywords indicate the type of query to be executed.

DISTINCT keyword can be used in the SELECT clause to return distinct values.
    Example:
    select distinct custom_field1 from _parts

FROM dataBaseObject:
    Which object to retrieve the data from. See link below for a list of available objects.

SET condition is used to change field values.
    The format is the name of the column followed by the "=" operator and then the value to set it to.
    Example:
    string1 = 'ABC-112A'

WHERE condition:
    Condition is field operator <field | value>
    Example:
    part_number = 'BL-5C'

    Logical operators can be used to group the conditions
    Example: field1 < 500 AND field2 = 'USD' OR field2 = 'EUR'

    Parenthesis can be used to change the precedence
    Example:
    field1 < 500 AND (field2 = 'USD' OR field2 = 'EUR')

    Conditional evaluation - a boolean value can be used with the AND to conditionally evaluate the predicate in the WHERE clause.
    Syntax: $eval AND field = value
    where 'eval' is a boolean variable in the script
    When 'eval' is true the predicate 'field = value' is used in the criteria
    When 'eval' is false the prediacate is ignored
    Example:
    e1 = true;
    e2 = false;
    rs = bmql("select... where $e1 AND f1 = v1 OR $e2 AND f2 = v2");

Operators:
    Relational operators: =, <>, <, >, <=, >=, LIKE, NOT LIKE, IN, NOT IN, IS NULL, IS NOT NULL
    Logical operators: AND, OR

ORDER BY clause is used to sort the data returned on the fields provided.
    Example:
    select part_number from _parts order by part_number

DESC keyword can be used to reverse the sort order to descending.
    Example:
    select part_number from _parts order by part_number desc

ASC can be used, optionally, to mean ascending sort order.

INTO is followed by a data table and then a list of columns (in parentheses and without quotes).
    These are the columns which the later values statement will populate.

VALUES prefixes a list of records to be inserted.
    Each record is bracketed by parentheses and contains a list of values to be inserted; the values must be given in the same order as the columns.
    String values must be single quoted.

    contextOverride (optional second parameter):
    This dictionary can be populated with the language context variable as a key and an
    overriding language as the value. When pulling data from the _parts table, this will
    substitute this language in, rather than the user's preferred language.

Supported Language Codes:
    Please see the product documentation for a complete list of supported languages and their corresponding codes.

    If the value for the requested language is blank, the site base language will be used instead. Additionally,
    if the requested language is not enabled or not found, the context variable will be ignored.

    Example:
    bmqlReturn = "nothing";
    Lang = dict("string");
    x_var = "de";
    put(Lang, "language", x_var);

    results = bmql("select description from _parts where part_number = 'Translations'", Lang);
    for result in results {
        bmqlReturn = get(result, "description");
    }
    return bmqlReturn;

    This will return the German description of the part Translations.

fieldMap (optional third parameter)
    This dictionary is a required field if variables are used within a where clause that is also a variable. Any variable used within a where clause that is a variable must also be defined in this parameter and referenced by the variable's key within the where clause.

    Example:
    lang = dict("string");
    fields = dict("string");
    x_var = "6.08";
    put(fields, "$field1", x_var);
    where = "float1 = $field1";
    results = bmql("select columnName from tableName where $where", lang, fields);

    Note: If the third parameter is used, the second parameter must also be defined.

Dynamic BMQL:
    You can use variables in the SELECT, FROM, VALUES and WHERE clause using $var syntax.
    Alternatively the entire WHERE clause can be a variable, as can the list of columns to be updated in an INTO statement. It must be a string.
    If there are variables in the WHERE clause variable, you must define these variables in a string Dictionary and pass them as a third parameter. In this case, you must also define a second parameter.

    Example:
    In this example, everything that can be dynamic is dynamic.

    bmqlReturn = "nothing";
    select = "string1,int1";
    from = "uploadXMLtable";
    lang = dict("string");
    fields = dict("string");
    x_var = "6.08";
    y_var = "2.03";
    a_var = 2;
    b_var = 1;
    put(fields, "$field1", x_var);
    set1 = "string1 = 'Platypus'";
    set2 = "string1 = 'Platypodes'";
    where = "float1 = $field1";
    where_delete = "string1 = $field1";
    results = bmql("insert into $from ($select) values ($x_var, $a_var),($y_var, $b_var)");
    results = bmql("delete from $from where $where_delete", lang, fields);
    results = bmql("update $from set $set1 where $where", lang, fields);
    results = bmql("modify $from set $set2 where $where", lang, fields);
    results = bmql("select $select from $from where $where", lang, fields);
    for result in results {
        bmqlReturn = get(result, "string1");
    }
    return bmqlReturn;

Note that INSERT, DELETE, UPDATE and MODIFY queries will only work on live data tables.

items.name: gettransaction
items.description: Retrieves, as a string, the transaction XML for a given transaction Id.
items.syntax: String gettransaction(Long bsId [, Json filterCriteria, Boolean includeRuleData])
items.example:
1. First parameter - bsId is a required parameter and refers to a transaction Id. If transaction with given Id doesn't exist, it throws an exception.

2. Second parameter - filterCriteria is an optional parameter in Json format. It can be used to return specific attributes for the main document and sub document respectively under <data_xml> node. It can also be used to return specific document numbers returned under <sub_documents> node.
The sample format of the optional Json parameter filterCriteria is as follows: json("{\"mainDoc\":{\"variableName\":\"quote\",\"returnSpecificAttributes\":\"quoteNum,quoteTotal\"},\"subDoc\":{\"variableName\":\"lineItem\",\"returnSpecificAttributes\":\"_price_quantity,_price_subtotal\",\"returnSpecificDocumentNumbers\":\"4,8,10\"}}").
If the optional parameter is passed in, then under mainDoc and subDoc, variableName of the mainDoc and subDoc is required. The specific attributes to be included in the transaction XML should be specified under returnSpecificAttributes. The specific documentNumbers that have to be returned in the transaction XML should be specified under returnSpecificDocumentNumbers.
If the optional parameter is not passed in, then the entire transaction is returned in the transaction XML.

3. Third parameter - includeRuleData, is an optional boolean parameter. If set to true, the evaluation data for constraints and access rules will be included in the transaction XML. If the parameter is not specified, its value defaults to false.
4. Transaction XML will be contained in <transaction> node. The result string will look like,
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<transaction><category>bm_cm_bs_data</category>...<num_transitions>5</num_transitions></transaction>

Example:

transactionXML = gettransaction(12345); // 12345 is a transaction id (bs id)

items.name: urldata
items.description: Retrieves data from a URL using HTTP GET or POST or PUT or PATCH depending on the parameter.  Deletes data from URL by invoking a service using DELETE depending on the parameter (see the makeurlparam function for formatting).  Note: If invocation of service is from the same site then Authorization is optional.
items.syntax: Dictionary urldata(String url, String httpMethod, [Dictionary headers, [String parameters, [Integer timeout, [Dictionary formData, [Boolean enableLoopback]]]]])
items.example:
On success, returns a Dictionary representation of an Http Response. The keys of the dictionary are response properties, like so:
  Key: "Status-Code", Value: "200 OK"
  Key(Header): "Content-Type", Value: "application/json"
  Key(Header): "Content-Length", Value: "2"
  Key(Body): "{}"
  
 An example of response handling.
  response = urldata(url, method, headers);
  print(get(response, "Status-Code")); // print the status code
  print(get(response, httpHeaderName)); // print the value of the header named httpHeaderName
  print(get(response, "Message-Body")); // print the message body
  
1. These are simple examples of how to create a request.
  
  Example: Send a GET request without a header
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>","GET");
  
  Example: Send a PUT request without authentication and JSON as payload
  headers=dict("string");
  put(headers, "Content-Type", "application/json");
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>","PUT",headers,{jsonBody});
  
  Example: Send a DELETE request with authentication and plain text payload
  headers=dict("string");
  encodecredential = encodebase64("<username>:<password>"); // for Authentication
  authstring="Basic " + encodecredential;
  put(headers, "Authorization", authstring); //optional if service is from the same site
  put(headers, "Content-Type", "text/plain");
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>","DELETE",headers,"request payload");
  
  Example: Send a PATCH request with authentication
  headers=dict("string");
  encodecredential = encodebase64("<username>:<password>"); // for Authentication
  authstring="Basic " + encodecredential;
  put(headers, "Authorization", authstring); //optional if service is from the same site
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>","PATCH",headers,{jsonBody});
  
2. An optional timeout parameter can be set on the urldata method. The timeout is in milliseconds. This overrides the General Site Option 'BML URL Function Timeout'.
  If there is a timeout, urldata() returns a dictionary representation of the error response, with Status-Code and Error-Message as keys.
  
  Example: Make a GET request with a timeout.
  headers=dict("string");
  put(headers, "content-type", "application/json");
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>", "GET",headers,"", 5000);
  
  Sample error message during timeout:
  {Status-Code=-1, Error-Message=Read timed out}
  
3. An optional dictionary parameter that represents form data can be set on the urldata method. This can be used to upload a file via the POST method. The dictionary must have the file name as the value for the key "filename" and the file contents as a byte array value for the key "filecontent". Any other form data string key,value pairs can also be set in the dictionary.
  
  Example: Make a POST request that uploads a file using form data.
  headers=dict("string");
  myData = "value1,value2,value3";
  fileContent=bytearray(myData);
  formData = dict("anytype");
  put(formData, "id", "id1");
  put(formData,"filename", "myData.csv");
  put(formData, "filecontent", fileContent);
  response=urldata("http://<hostname>/<path>", "POST",headers,"", 5000, formData);
  
4. If the executing user is logged in to an integrated site, then calls to that integrated site can use the user's authentication token. To do this, a string token ("$_access_token_salesforce$" for Salesforce and "$_access_token_dynamics365$" for Microsoft Dynamics365) can be inserted into a header value. When the call is executed, this token will be replaced with the user's partner authentication token.
  
  Example: Request a list of Salesforce sobjects
  headers=dict("string");
  put(headers, "Authorization", "Bearer $_access_token_salesforce$");
  response=urldata("https://<salesforcehost>/services/data/v37.0", "GET", headers);
  
  Example: Request a list of Microsoft Dynamics Opportunities.
  headers=dict("string");
  put(headers, "Authorization", "Bearer $_access_token_dynamics365$");
  response=urldata("https://<dynamicshost>/api/data/v8.2/opportunities", GET, headers);
5. Additional identifier needs to be used to make outbound calls to the resource registered with OAuth Provider . To do this, a string token ("$_access_token_oauthprovider$" ) can be inserted into a header value. When the call is executed, this token will be replaced with the access token obtained from the OAuth Provider based on the setup in integration center. If call requires user identity , corresponding identifier("UserIdentity") can be inserted else if not inserted, it is treated as without user identity propagation. For certain OAuth Provider like IDCS identifier "scope" needs to be passed. Scope value needs to be obtained from resource APIs documentation
  
  Example: Intregrate with external resource registered with OAuth Provider
  headers=dict("string");
  put(headers, "Authorization", "Bearer $_access_token_oauthprovider$");
  put(headers, "UserIdentity", "<string>");
  put(headers, "Scope", "<allowed scope registred with client >");
  response=urldata("https://<resourceendpoint>", "GET", headers);
6. An optional Boolean parameter can be passed in for enableLoopback, defaults to true, if you want request to same site to go out internet and come back , set to false.

urldatabypost("http://www.example.com", "a1=v1&a2=v2", "", dict("string"), true, 5000); //Uses optional timeout with returnErrorResponse set to true

3. sortType takes the string values "text", "numeric", or "date". A string array with no sortType will be sorted with numbers first, capitals etters next, then lower case. Numbers are treated as strings: they are sorted by the first digit, then subsequent digits.

items.name: applytemplate
items.description: Applies Dictionary payload and JSON context to the template file, where JSON takes precedence over payload.
items.syntax: String applytemplate(String templateFileLocation [, Dictionary payload [, String defaultErrorMessage[, Json jsonIdentifier]]])
items.example:
This function will return a String that represents the result of applying a set of token key/value pairs to the template file.
This set of token key/value pairs can come from either an explicitly user defined map, JSON
or implicitly imported rule input variables from System, Main Document or Sub Document.

Overwrite an imported rule input variable:
1. Overwrite globally - To overwrite an imported rule input variable,
user can use the imported rule input variable name as the key in the user map.
This value from the user map will be applied globally to either main document or sub document within the template.
2. Overwrite locally - To overwrite an imported rule input variable within a specific document,
user can use a prefix of "[documentNumber]~" (e.g. 1~) on the imported rule input variable name as the key in the user map.
NOTE: Overwrite locally has higher precedence than overwrite globally.

The tokens in the template file should start with "{{" and end with "}}" signs.
Below is the list of valid formats and features:
1. {{YOUR_TOKEN_HERE}}
This token will be replaced by the string value
defined by the key "YOUR_TOKEN_HERE" in the input payload dictionary
2. {{#each <SubDocumentVariableName>}} {{/each}}
Used for looping through the instances of a SubDocument.
For example, the SubDocumentVariableName is "lineItem",
attributes "_price_subtotal" and "_price_net_price" of the lineItem
had been manually imported as rule inputs in the BML scripts.
To reference those attributes within the template, user can do:
{{#each lineItem}}
<Line>
<PriceSubTotal>{{_price_subtotal}}</PriceSubTotal>
<PriceNetPrice>{{_price_net_price}}</PriceNetPrice>
</Line>
{{/each}}
3. {{#if YOUR_NOT_NULL_STRING_VALUE_HERE}} {{/if}}
Conditional statement. For example, given template
"{{#if _type}}<Line><PriceSubTotal>{{_price_subtotal}}</PriceSubTotal></Line>{{/if}}":
If variable "_type" contains value "RECURRING", then above template will be rendered.
If variable "_type" contains value "" or null, then nothing will be rendered for above template.
4. {{formatDateString context originalFormat newFormat}}
Used to format context dateString from original format to the new format.
Context: current date string. OriginalFormat: format used for current date string.
NewFormat: the format the output use. Return: dateString using the new format.
The format follows the
<a href="http://docs.oracle.com/javase/6/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html">java SimpleDateFormat patterns.</a>
5. {{#equal context compareTo}}{{else}}{{/equal}}
Equal block statement. If context equals to compareTo, then the template before the {{else}} will be rendered, otherwise the {{else}} will be rendered.
For example, "{{#equal price_type "RECURRING"}}<recurringprice>{{_recurringprice}}</recurringprice>{{else}}Price type is not recurring.{{/equal}}":
If variable "price_type" is "RECURRING", then above template will be rendered as <recurringprice>34</recurringprice>.
If variable "price_type" is not "RECURRING", then "Price type is not recurring." will be rendered.
NOTE: the {{else}} is optional.

Other processing rules:
1. Input payload should contain value of type String for each key.
2. All the variable and token names are not case sensitive.
3. There must be token specified within the {{}}, or error message will be returned.
4. Token in the template should not contain "~" sign, or error message will be returned.
5. If there is a token specified within the {{}}, e.g. {{NO_TOKEN_VALUE_DEFINED}},
but no value is defined in both the input payload and the imported variables, nothing will be rendered for this token.
6. The returned error message is not translated.
7. Special characters (e.g. &) will not display correctly in the debugger.
8. JSON keys are case sensitive and should match with the template token case.
9. To override any of the system , Main Doc or Sub Document variables, Keys should be present as first level keys in JSON.
10. If LineItem (sub document variable Name) is overridden in JSON, then any of the sub document keys with or without TILDE will not have the significance.
11. Key with TILDE(~) in User Defined Map will be considered as priority over the same JSON key without TILDE.

Example:

(Template file test.txt content)
This is user defined variable VAR1, value = {{VAR1}}.
This is user defined variable VAR2, value = {{VAR2}}.
This is user defined variable VAR3, value = {{VAR3}}.

(BML script)
templateFileLocation = "$BASE_PATH$/ApplytemplateTest/test.txt";
payload = dict("string");
put(payload, "VAR1", "Hello world");
put(payload, "VAR2", "Payload VAR2");
jsonobj = json("{\"VAR2\":\"json var2 value\",\"VAR3\":\"json var3 value\"}");
output = applytemplate(templateFileLocation, payload,"",jsonobj);
return output;

(Result)
This is user defined variable VAR1, value = Hello world.
This is user defined variable VAR2, value = json var2 value.
This is user defined variable VAR3, value = json var3 value.

items.name: readxmlsingle
items.description: Reads a set of single XML node content based on a set of XPath expressions.
items.syntax: Dictionary readxmlsingle(String xmlPayload, String[] xpaths [, String defaultErrorMessage])
items.example:
This function will return a BMLDictionary where the String keys are the input xpaths and String values are the XPath evaluation results for the input xpaths.
This function will return a BMLDictionary that contains error message when there is any error occurred. The key for the error message in the BMLDictionary is "BM_READXMLSINGLE_ERROR".

Processing Rules:
1. If a given XPath is evaluated as a single node in result,
the returned String content is based on the node type and content:
1.1. Result is an ATTRIBUTE_NODE - The ATTRIBUTE_NODE value is returned
1.2. Result is a node that contains text content in its child nodes -
The concatenated node values from TEXT nodes and CDATA nodes,
if they contain not-empty text, is returned as the content of the node.
NOTE: A node that contains white space only will be ignored.
NOTE: EntityRef nodes are not processed due to DTD is not allowed.
NOTE: Any element nodes in the sublist is ignored.
1.3. Result is a node that does not contain text content in its child nodes -
A String representation of the node (XML fragment) will be returned.
NOTE: A node that contains white space only will be ignored.
2. If a given XPath is evaluated as multiple ATTRIBUTE_NODE or ELEMENT_NODE in result,
only the first node string content will be returned based on above String contents retrieving rules.
3. To avoid abuse usage of the namespace prefix, the input argument xmlPayload should not contain
namespace prefixes for more than 1000, or IllegalArgumentException will be returned.
4. There are three ways to define namespaces in a document:
Default namespaces, No namespace, and Namespaces with prefixes.
4.1. If the input XML document contains default namespaces,
but the default namespace is not on the root,
then the element(s) in such default namespace will be ignored.
4.2. If the input XML document contains default namespace that is on the root,
then the input XPath for these default namespace elements should contain a namespace prefix "BM_NS".
The returned evaluated result will contain the namespace attribute information if the return is a XML fragment.
4.3. If the input XML document contains no namespaces, no namespace prefix is needed in the input XPath.
4.4. If the input XML document contains namespaces with prefixes, namespace prefix is needed in the input XPath.
The returned evaluated result will contain the namespace attribute information if the return is a XML fragment.
5. The returned error message is not translated.

Example:
(BML script)
xmlPayload = "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?><library><book lang=\"en\">Spring in Action</book></library>";
xpaths = string[1];
xpaths[0] = "/library/book[1]/@lang";
output = readxmlsingle(xmlPayload, xpaths);
for xpath in xpaths
{ print("(key, value) = (" + xpath + ", " + get(output, xpath) + ")"); }
return "";

(Output)
(key, value) = (/library/book[1]/@lang, en)

items.name: jsonget
items.description: Returns a JSON object value for a given key.
items.syntax: <ValueType> jsonget(Json jsonIdentifier, String key [, String valueType [, <ValueType> defaultValue]])
items.example:
1. Returns the value from a JSON object for the given key.

2. The valueType and defaultValue parameters are optional.

3. The returned value is converted to a data type equal to the valueType parameter, which is String by default.

4. The defaultValue parameter is returned if the given key is not available.

5. null is returned if: the given key is not available AND valueType is String, JSON, or JSON array AND defaultValue is not provided.

6. An error is thrown if:
    (a) the returned value could not be converted to the data type of valueType.
    (b) the defaultValue parameter's data type is not the same as valueType parameter.
    (c) the given key is not available AND valueType is Integer, Float, or Boolean AND defaultValue is not provided.

Example:

str = "{\"key1\":\"mystring\",\"key2\": 10,\"key3\":2.9,\"key4\":[\"v1\",\"v2\"],\"key5\":true,\"key6\":{\"key7\":\"val7\",\"key8\":\"val8\"}}";
jsonObj = json(str);

/* Get string (two parameters) */
valStr1 = jsonget(jsonObj,"key2");
print valStr1;
//Output: 10

/* Get string (three parameters) */
valStr2 = jsonget(jsonObj,"key1","string");
print valStr2;
//Output: mystring

/* Get integer */
valInt = jsonget(jsonObj,"key2","integer");
print valInt;
//Output: 10

/* Get float */
valFloat = jsonget(jsonObj,"key3","float");
print valFloat;
//Output: 2.9

/* Get boolean */
valBoolean = jsonget(jsonObj,"key5","boolean");
print valBoolean;
//Output: true

/* Get jsonarray */
valJsonArray = jsonget(jsonObj,"key4","jsonarray");
print valJsonArray;
//Output: ["v1","v2"]

/* Get json */
valJson = jsonget(jsonObj,"key6","json");
print valJson;
//Output: {"key7":"val7","key8":"val8"}

/* Get default value */
defaultVal1 = jsonget(jsonObj,"key10","string","defaultValue");
print defaultVal1;
//Output: defaultValue

/* Get default value */
defaultVal2 = jsonget(jsonObj,"key10","string");
print defaultVal2;
//Output: null

/* Get default value */
defaultVal3 = jsonget(jsonObj,"key10","integer");
print defaultVal3;
//An error is thrown because key10 is not found and the type is integer.

1. Inserts a new key-value entry into a JSON object.

2. If the given key already exists in the JSON object, its corresponding value will be updated to the given value.

3. The inserted/updated value is returned.

items.name: jsonarrayget

str = "[\"mystring\",10,2.9,[\"v1\",\"v2\"],true,{\"key7\":\"val7\",\"key8\":\"val8\"}]";

items.name: jsonpathremove
items.description: Removes the value(s)/object(s) corresponding to a given JSON path from a JSON object and returns a boolean value.
items.example:
1. Removes the value(s)/object(s) from a JSON object corresponding to a given JSON path.

2. true is returned if the node(s) corresponding to the given path is successfully removed.

3. false is returned if a node corresponding to the given path could not be found.

4. If there are multiple JSON path nodes corresponding to the given path, all corresponding nodes are removed.

5. An exception is thrown if the JSON path syntax is not correct.

6. Because this function supports object references, caution is recommended while removing objects (JSON, JSON array).

Example:

str = "{\"key1\":null,\"key2\":\"str\",\"key3\":90}";
jsonObj = json(str);

remVal1 = jsonpathremove(jsonObj,"$..key1");
print remVal1;
//Output: true

print jsonObj;
//Output: {"key2":"str","key3":90}

remVal2 = jsonpathremove(jsonObj,"$..key999");
print remVal2;
//Output: false

print jsonObj;
//Output: {"key2":"str","key3":90}

items.name: jsonpathgetsingle
items.description: Returns the value corresponding to a given JSON path from a JSON object.
items.syntax: <ValueType> jsonpathgetsingle(Json jsonIdentifier, String jsonPath [, String valueType [, <ValueType> defaultValue]])
items.example:
1. Returns the value from a JSON object corresponding to a given JSON path.

2. The valueType and defaultValue parameters are optional.

3. The returned value is converted to a data type equal to the valueType parameter, which is String by default.

4. The defaultValue parameter is returned if the given JSON path is not found.

5. null is returned if: the given JSON path is not found AND valueType is String, JSON, or JSON array AND defaultValue is not provided.

6. An error is thrown if:
    (a) there are multiple values corresponding to the given JSON path.
    (a) the returned value could not be converted to the data type of valueType.
    (b) the defaultValue parameter's data type is not the same as valueType parameter.
    (c) the given JSON path is not found AND valueType is Integer, Float, or Boolean AND defaultValue is not provided.

Example:

str = "{\"store\":{\"book\":[{\"category\":\"reference\",\"author\":\"Nigel Rees\"},{\"category\":\"fiction\",\"author\":\"Evelyn Waugh\"}]},\"expensive\":10}";
jsonObj = json(str);

catArray = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[0]");
print catArray;
//Output: {"category":"reference","author":"Nigel Rees"}

expenseInt = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.expensive","integer");
print expenseInt;
//Output: 10

expenseStr = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.expensive","string");
print expenseStr;
//Output: 10

title = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[0].title","string");
print title;
//Output: null

price = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[0].price","float");
print price;
//An error is thrown because the JSON path is not found and valueType is float.

firstBook = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[0]","json");
print firstBook;
//Output: {"category":"reference","author":"Nigel Rees"}

defaultVal1 = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[100]","json",json());
print defaultVal1;
//Output: {}

defaultVal2 = jsonpathgetsingle(jsonObj,"$.store.book[0].location","string","unknown");
print defaultVal2;
//Output: unknown

items.name: jsoncopy

items.example:
1. Creates a copy of a JSON object.

2. All child nodes of the JSON object are copied and a similar hierarchy is created.

3. Any changes made to the original JSON object will not impact the copied JSON object.

Example:

str = "{\"key1\":null,\"key2\":\"str\",\"key3\":90}";
jsonObj = json(str);

copyObj = jsoncopy(jsonObj);
print copyObj;
//Output: {"key1":null,"key2":"str","key3":90}

jsonremove(jsonObj,"key1");

print copyObj;

items.name: jsonarraycopy

items.example:
1. Creates a copy of a JSON array object.

2. All objects in the array are copied and a similar hierarchy is created.

3. Any changes made to the original JSON array object will not impact the copied JSON array object.

Example:

str = "[\"string\",1,2.3,{\"key1\":\"val1\"},[1,2,3],true,false]";
jsonArrObj = jsonarray(str);

items.name: jsonpathcheck
items.description: Checks if a JSON path is found in a JSON object and returns a boolean value.
items.example:
1. Checks if a JSON path is found in a JSON object.

2. true is returned if the JSON path is found.

3. false is returned if the JSON path is not found or if the JSON object is null.

4. An error is thrown if the JSON path is invalid.

Example:

str = "{\"store\":{\"book\":[{\"category\":\"reference\",\"author\":\"Nigel Rees\"},{\"category\":\"fiction\",\"author\":\"Evelyn Waugh\"}]},\"expensive\":10}";

items.name: jsonpathset
items.description: Updates all nodes corresponding to a given JSON path in a JSON object with a value and returns a string array of the nodes that were updated.
items.syntax: String[] jsonpathset(Json jsonIdentifier, String jsonPath, <ValueType> value)
items.example:
1. Updates all nodes corresponding to a given JSON path in a JSON object with a value.

2. A string containing all updated absolute/normalized JSON path nodes is returned.

3. An empty string array is returned if a node corresponding to the JSON path is not found.

4. null is returned if the object at the JSON path node is null or the JSON path is invalid.

Example:

str = "{\"key1\":90,\"key2\":[{\"key1\":900}],\"key3\":{\"key1\":9000}}";
jsonObj1 = json(str);
jsonObj2 = json("{\"key1\":89}");
jsonObj3 = json("{\"key2\":\"val2\"}");
jsonObj4 = json("{\"key1\":89}");

jsonPath1 = jsonpathset(jsonObj1,"$..key1",true);
print jsonPath1;
//Output: [$['key1'],$['key2'][0]['key1'],$['key3']['key1']]

print jsonObj1;
//Output: {"key1":true,"key2":[{"key1":true}],"key3":{"key1":true}}

jsonPath2 = jsonpathset(jsonObj2,"$..key1",jsonObj3);
print jsonPath2;
//Output: [$['key1']]

print jsonObj2;
//Output: {"key1":{"key2":"val2"}}

jsonput(jsonObj3,"key3","val2");
print jsonObj3;
//Output: {"key2":"val2","key3":"val2"}

jsonPath3 = jsonpathset(jsonObj4,"$..key3",jsonObj3);
print jsonPath3;
//Output: []

str2 = "{\"key\":[{\"value\":9},{\"value\":90},{\"value\":900},{\"value\":9000}]}";
jsonObj5 = json(str2);
jsonPath4 = jsonpathset(jsonObj5,"$.key[1:3].value",true);
print jsonPath4;
//output: [$['key'][1]['value'], $['key'][2]['value']]

print jsonObj5;
//output: {"key":[{"value":9},{"value":true},{"value":true},{"value":9000}]}
//$.key[1:3].value Updates nodes from index 1 (inclusive) until index 3 (exclusive)

items.name: jsonpathgetmultiple
items.description: Returns the value(s)/path(s) corresponding to a given JSON path from a JSON object.
items.syntax: JsonArray jsonpathgetmultiple(Json jsonIdentifier, String jsonPath [, Boolean asPath])
items.example:
1. Returns the value(s)/path(s) from a JSON object corresponding to a given JSON path.

2. The asPath parameter is optional and its default value is false.

3. A JSON array containing all object values corresponding to the given JSON path is returned if the asPath parameter is false.

4. A JSON array containing all nodes corresponding to the give JSON path is returned if the asPath parameter is true.

Example:

str = "{\"key1\":90,\"key2\":[{\"key1\":900}],\"key3\":{\"key1\":9000}}";
jsonObj = json(str);

arrayVals = jsonpathgetmultiple(jsonObj,"$..key1");

pathValue = jsonpathgetmultiple(jsonObj2,"$..key[1:3].value");

//Output: [90,900]
//$..key[1:3] All keys from index 1 (inclusive) until index 3 (exclusive)

items.name: jsonarrayrefid
items.description: Returns a unique reference ID that represents the input JSON array.
items.example:
1. Can only be invoked by Commerce advanced modify, auto update or advanced default functions.
2. Provides a more efficient method to pass a JSON array to the BML output to update an array set.

Example:

// feeJsonArray is a JSON array
// feeArraySet is the main doc array set variable name
// To update feeArraySet, jsonarrayrefid is more efficient than jsonarraytostr when the JSON array is large

items.example:
1. bsId is the commerce transaction ID.

2. lineNumber is the the document number of the model line, also acting as the root BOM line in the quote.

3. lineFields are the additional line attributes to be fetched from the quote lines and stored in the returned BOM instance.
   It is optional parameter and if it is not provided the default value will be null.

4. validateBomModel is used for whether to validate the returned BOM against the latest BOM item definition.
   The validation verifies the BOM instance tree against the BOM item definition based on part numbers and hierarchy.
   It populates the BOM item variable names,may correct the BOM instance hierarchy according to the latest definition, and exclude items that are no longer part of the latest definition.
   It is optional parameter and if it is not provided the default value will be true.

5. flattenChildItems is used for whether to flatten the children items. If true, all descendant BOM items are stored as the direct children of the returned root BOM item.
   It is optional parameter and if it is not provided the default value will be false.

6. isSalesBom is used for whether the returned BOM should be a sales BOM or a manufacturing BOM.
   It is optional parameter and if it is not provided the default value will be true.

Example:
bsId=18430319;
jObj = getbom(bsId, 2);
print jObj;

items.name: throwerror
items.description: This function is used to throw business logic and system exceptions.
items.example:
This function stops the execution of the BML script and displays an error message to the user. The error can be of type business logic or system error. In case of system error, a generic message will be displayed and the actual message will be logged to the error log file.
Note: This function should not be used in config or commerce rule conditions as message will not be adequately displayed to the user.

1. The first parameter is a customized error message that is printed exactly as entered by the user, regardless of the language character set used.
2. The second parameter is optional with default value as false. If set to true then the error message will be treated as system error.

Case 1:
throwerror("This is a custom error!!");

Message displayed to the user "This is a custom error!!"

Case 2:
throwerror("This is a system error!!",true);

Message displayed to the user "An unknown error has occurred. Please contact system administrator."

Error log contains the message "This is a system error!!".

items.name: globaldictset
items.description: Adds or updates key-value pair to global cache.
items.syntax: String globaldictset(String key, String value[, Integer minTimeToLive [, Boolean isolate]])
items.example:
1. The first parameter is the key which is of type String.
2. The second parameter is the value which is of type String.
3. The third parameter specifies the minimum time, in minutes, the key-value pair is guaranteed to exist in the global cache.
4. minTimeToLive is optional and default value is 1440 minutes (1 day).
5. minTimeToLive should be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 525600 minutes(365 days).
6. The fourth parameter isolate which is of type Boolean.
7. isolate parameter, if this has been set to true Transaction boundary will be isolated from other transaction.
8. If key is null or empty, unique key will be generated and added to global cache.
9. If key is already present, the provided value will be updated for the corresponding key.
10. This BML function returns the key added to the global cache.
11. This function is independent of user session.

Example:
storedkey = globaldictset("key1", "value1"); //mintimeToLive will be defaulted to 1440
print storedkey;
//Output: key1
storedkey2 = globaldictset("", "value2", 1000); // This record will be removed by the next scheduled batch that runs after 1000 mins
print storedkey2; // unique key will be generated and returned.
storedkey3 = globaldictset("key3", "some value", true); // This record will be added in isolated transaction and mintimeToLive will default to 1440
print storedkey3; // Output: key3
storedkey4 = globaldictset("key4", "some value", 1000, true); // This record will be added in isolated transaction
print storedkey4; // Output: key4

items.name: addpartstotransaction
items.description: Adds Part Line Items to the Transaction.
items.syntax: JsonArray addpartstotransaction(JsonArray<Json&gt parts[, String priceBookVarName[, String[] resultAttributeArray[, String pricingTriggerPoint]]])
items.example:
1. The first parameter is a JsonArray of Json objects.
A Part Json object example:
{
"partNumber": "part1",
"quantity": 1,
"price": 3.50,
"parentDocNumber": 2
}

"price" and "parentDocNumber" are both optional.

2. The second(optional) parameter is a String value for setting the Transaction Price Book, if not already set.

3. The third(optional) parameter is a String[] for providing document attributes in the result Json.

Example:
["_part_quantity", "_document_number", "_part_number", "_price_item_price_each", "myAttribute"]

will result in a response similar to the following when adding 1 part:

[{"_part_quantity":"1", "_document_number":"2", "_part_number":"part1", "_price_item_price_each":"3.50", "myAttribute":"my custom value"}]

4. The fourth(optional) parameter is a String value to specify when the added line items should be priced: "beforeInsert", "afterInsert", "none". If the parameter is absent or empty, pricing is executed both before and after insertion of the line items.

Other Examples:

Example 1:
resultArray = jsonarray(); // function return is json array

partObj = json(); // part data is json object
jsonput(partObj , "partNumber", "part1");
jsonput(partObj , "quantity", 1);

inputArray = jsonarray(); // parts to add should be added to json array
jsonarrayappend(inputArray , partObj );

resultArray = addpartstotransaction(inputArray, "_default_price_book");

print(resultArray); // prints: [{"_document_number":"2", "_part_number":"part1", "_price_quantity":"1", "_price_list_price_each":"3.50", "_parent_doc_number":""}]

Example 2:
resultArray = jsonarray();

part1 = json();
jsonput(part1 , "partNumber", "part1");
jsonput(part1 , "quantity", 1);

part2 = json();
jsonput(part2 , "partNumber", "part2");
jsonput(part2 , "quantity", 2);
jsonput(part2 , "price", 4.50); // overrides price

part3 = json();
jsonput(part3 , "partNumber", "part3");
jsonput(part3 , "quantity", 3);
jsonput(part3 , "parentDocNumber", 2); // adds part as child of parent

inputArray = jsonarray();
jsonarrayappend(inputArray , part1 );
jsonarrayappend(inputArray , part2 );
jsonarrayappend(inputArray , part3 );

resultAttributeArray = string[5]; // defines the attributes to return
resultAttributeArray[0] = "_document_number";
resultAttributeArray[1] = "_part_number";
resultAttributeArray[2] = "_price_quantity";
resultAttributeArray[3] = "_price_list_price_each";
resultAttributeArray[4] = "_parent_doc_number";

resultArray = addpartstotransaction(inputArray, resultAttributeArray);

print(resultArray);
// prints: [
// {"_document_number":"3", "_part_number":"part1", "_price_quantity":"1", "_price_list_price_each":"3.5", "_parent_doc_number":""},
// {"_document_number":"4", "_part_number":"part2", "_price_quantity":"2", "_price_list_price_each":"4.5", "_parent_doc_number":""},
// {"_document_number":"5", "_part_number":"part3", "_price_quantity":"3", "_price_list_price_each":"3.5", "_parent_doc_number":"2"}
//]

Example 3: Similar to Example 1 and 2, but with pricing triggered after insertion of price item.
resultArray = jsonarray(); // function return is json array

partObj = json(); // part data is json object
jsonput(partObj , "partNumber", "part1");
jsonput(partObj , "quantity", 1);

inputArray = jsonarray(); // parts to add should be added to json array

items.name: generatehmacmessage
items.description: Converts the input message to a HMAC generated string using a secret key.
items.syntax: String generatehmacmessage(String inputmessage, String key [, String algorithm])
items.example:
This function computes a Hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) from a cryptographic hash function using a secret key for given input message. A HMAC is a small set of data that helps authenticate the nature of message. It protects the integrity and the authenticity of the message.
This function takes 3 arguments:
1. inputmessage - string : Message that needs to be HMAC generated
2. key - string : Secret Key
3. algorithm - (optional) string : Cryptographic hash algorithm for HMAC generation
Available algorithms:
a. SHA256 (Default)
b. SHA384
c. SHA512
d. SHA1
e. MD5
NOTE: This parameter is case-sensitive.

Example:
1. inputmessage = "This is an input example for HMAC authentication.";
key = "cfthsnkjsavjiCe=";
hmac = generatehmacmessage(inputmessage,key); //uses Default algorithm- SHA256
print(hmac);
//prints cec5cc9241a2529a0de2b1b4cb250738ef52ae5f8bf6db9034bd4dbf4e37bee6

2. inputmessage = "This is an input example for HMAC authentication.";
key = "cfthsnkjsavjiCe=";
algo = "MD5";
hmac = generatehmacmessage(inputmessage, key, algo);
print(hmac);
//prints eaf3702517fef48d3f114f32a3c3394b

3. The second or third(optional) parameter is a String[] for providing document attributes in the result Json.
